name: Mattenai
overview: Mattenai was a male figure noted in the book of Ezra as a descendant of Hashum who had married a foreign wife. The biblical record does not specify his tribe or other personal details beyond this unique attribute. His mention highlights issues related to intermarriage among the post-exilic community in Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Mattenai means 'gift' and is a proper name recorded in Ezra 10:33. This name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries the common Hebrew meaning of a gift, reflecting a typical naming practice of the period.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Mattenai as a descendant of Hashum, establishing a clear familial link. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded in the biblical text for Mattenai.
scriptureSignificance: Mattenai's significance in Scripture lies in his representation of the challenges faced by the returning exiles who intermarried with foreign wives, a situation addressed in Ezra 10. His lineage from Hashum ties him to a post-exilic community striving to maintain covenant faithfulness. The mention of Mattenai underscores the biblical concern for purity of the Israelite community and obedience to God's commands during the restoration period.
